newsitem.title: USA: US cash crude markets mixed for end of Apr grades.
newsitem.headline: US cash crude markets mixed for end of Apr grades.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes quietly traded late Tuesday for April barrels, while outright prices retraced slight losses after the release of weekly inventory data by the American Petroleum Institute (API).
Differentials for April domestic grades fluctuated on pipeline scheduling day, ending trade for the prompt month.
"It looked like people were looking to see the end of April business before getting interested in anything else," said one cash trader, noting the mild tone in the market.
May West Texas Intermediate/Cushing lost around 5 cents before API data was released, pegged at $20.95-$21.05 a barrel.
Late talk in the April/May WTI roll was around -5 cts, putting the late April WTI/Cushing at $20.90-$21.00 a barrel.
The roll traded to a peak of +13 cts earlier in the session, moving quickly between the two ends of a 15-20 cts trading range.

Grade differentials moved lower for April Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James, where deals were heard some 50-65 cts below the benchmark. Traders said the numbers narrowed later in the day, but pegging an accurate count for April barrels was made difficult by a lack of volume and mopping-up dealings.

May LLS talked quietly, reportedly getting sold at a 35 cts discount to the WTI/Cushing. Traders said the influx of Brent and West African barrels to the U.S. Gulf continued to apply pressure to domestic sweets.
Sour grades were also under pressure on renewed talk that Iraqi crude-holder Coastal Corp was showing Basrah Light at May WTI -$2.40 for mid-May arrival to the U.S. Gulf.
West Texas Sour/Midland deals were seen for May barrels at discounts of $2.45 and $2.50 to the WTI/Cushing, with talk late at $2.50-55 under the marker.
Traders said May Postings were stagnant around a $1.75 value all session, with April Postings closer to $1.55-60.
API statistics showed U.S. crude stocks falling 2.2 million barrels for the week ended March 21, with distillates also down 1.34 million barrels and gasoline stocks up 226,000 barrels.
